claims.text: The baseline TiVNbTa alloy is a single-phase homogeneous BCC material.
Baseline TiVNbTa has a yield strength of about 330 MPa at 1273 K.
Baseline TiVNbTa has a compressive strength of about 423 MPa at 1273 K.
Baseline TiVNbTa accommodates approximately 40% strain at room temperature.
Severe plastic deformation followed by two-stage annealing and addition of minor grain-boundary pinning agents will create a stabilized bimodal TiVNbTa microstructure.
Annealing at approximately 600°C will stabilize the ultrafine grains introduced by severe plastic deformation.
A subsequent anneal at approximately 900°C will produce a coarser grain fraction.
The resulting microstructure will contain both fine-grained and coarse-grained fractions.
The fine-grained fraction will improve high-temperature strength through grain-boundary strengthening that hinders dislocation motion.
The coarse-grained fraction will preserve overall ductility.
Minor grain-boundary pinning agents will retard grain coarsening during prolonged high-temperature exposure.
Retarding grain coarsening will stabilize the bimodal microstructure and maintain enhanced mechanical properties.
The processed alloy will have a yield strength greater than 330 MPa at 1273 K.
The processed alloy will maintain ductility after its high-temperature strength is increased.
The enhanced performance will persist at operating temperatures up to 1273 K.
The processed alloy will be compatible with the interfacial thermal-expansion ranges of W and CuCrZr.
Preserving microstructural stability will ensure effective thermal management between W and CuCrZr.
